newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Mandela satisfied Zaire rebel advance on hold.
newsitem.headline: Mandela satisfied Zaire rebel advance on hold.

text.p: South African President Nelson Mandela said on Wednesday he was satisfied that Zaire rebel leader Laurent Kabila was honouring an undertaking made three days ago to halt his army's march on the capital, Kinshasa.

Mandela said his deputy, Thabo Mbeki, had asked Kabila on Tuesday about reports that the rebels were closing in on Kinshasa despite Kabila's pledge to halt the advance pending the departure from power of President Mobutu Sese Seko.

"He (Kabila) told the deputy president that he honoured the undertaking that he gave to us and that his troops have not advanced at all since he gave that order (last Sunday)," Mandela told reporters in Cape Town.
"Nothing has happened to make me believe that the undertaking is now not being honoured."

With reliable battlefront reports hard to come by and conflicting propaganda claims proliferating, it was not clear whether rebel units were indeed marking time and simply holding their positions, or continuing their advance on Kinshasa.
